newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti shares rise 8.5 pct in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti shares rise 8.5 pct in Milan.

text.p: Shares in Italian information technology group Olivetti leapt 8.53 percent higher to 505 lire at the start of trade in Milan.
The stock immediately pared gains to drop below the 500 lire per share level however, trading 5.31 percent up at 490 lire by 1018 GMT on turnover of 11 million shares.

The start of trading in the shares of the crisis-ridden company had been delayed two hours from the normal bourse opening time after Olivetti released the answers to 16 questions posed by stock market regulator Consob on the state of the group's finances.

Olivetti furnished the market with little information in its response, saying in a statement earlier on Wednesday it could not divulge confidential information about negotiations under way on future divestments or strategic accords.

It also said it could not state its consolidated financial situation for the end of August 1996 until the first week of October. This was because of the need to gather "data coming from around 200 companies operating in the group."
Brokers said investors had now stepped back after selling the share heavily in recent days and were following developments.

"There's nothing particularly new in the 16 answers. People are watching and keeping their distance. We haven't really got much more information than what we had yesterday evening," one broker here said.
Another factor staying players' hands was the expectation of an extraordinary board meeting which newspapers and industry sources said had been called for later on Wednesday.
